Apple updated the Mac mini and Mac Studio today, adding Wi-Fi 7 support to both product lines for the first time. Below is the complete list of Apple devices that support all Wi-Fi 7 features.

6 GHz band operation not available in all regions

Apple today published a support document detailing which of its products fully support Wi-Fi 7.

This list differs from Apple's broader list of devices that can "connect to a Wi-Fi 7 network," since Wi-Fi 7 is backward compatible.

That means devices that only support Wi-Fi 6E can still join a compatible Wi-Fi 7 network and use the 6 GHz band where applicable, but they won't get the full suite of Wi-Fi 7 features.

That said, here's the list of devices Apple officially says support all Wi-Fi 7 features as of August 2026:

  • MacBook Pro with M5 Pro or M5 Max chip or later
  • MacBook Air with M5 chip or later
  • Mac mini with M5 Pro chip or later
  • Mac Studio with M5 Max chip or later
  • iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro Max, or later (not including iPhone 16e, iPhone 17e)
  • iPhone Air
  • iPad Pro with M5 chip or later
  • iPad Air with M4 chip or later

Apple notes that "Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 7 functionality over the 6 GHz band is offered only in countries and regions where the spectrum is allowed for unlicensed Wi-Fi use," adding that "if your local regulator hasn't approved this operation, your device will use Wi-Fi only over the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands."
